subject: POC: Hands-on throughput playback & prompt routing session
messages:
From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@optiscale.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Cara Lin <cara@optiscale.com>
Date: 2028-07-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC kickoff — availability and high-level asks

Thanks for the quick reply, Diego — excited to get this started. A few asks from our side so we can shape the hands-on session:

- Primary goal: validate throughput at ~4k tokens/sec sustained for our multi-tenant prompt fanout (16 concurrent users).
- Latency SLO: p95 < 250ms for single-turn prompts at 256 tokens.
- Environment: we'll bring a representative prompt set (Q&A + instruction-following) and one warm cache scenario.
- We need a short walkthrough of how routing policies will fall back to smaller quantized models.

Preferred dates: week of July 24 or July 31, ideally a 3-hour block for workshop + 1-hour load test window.

I'll attach the baseline prompt bundle and a short doc with their request details.

—Alex
Alex Mercer
Director of Engineering, OptiScale
[Attachment: optiscale-prompt-bundle.zip (zip)]

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@optiscale.com>
Cc: Cara Lin <cara@optiscale.com>
Date: 2028-07-16T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC kickoff — availability and high-level asks

Alex — thanks, this is exactly the kind of detail we need. July 31 looks best from our side. Proposed plan:

1) 09:00–09:30 PT: 15-minute intros + scope alignment
2) 09:30–11:00 PT: Hands-on prompt review and routing config (prompt playback, KV cache priming)
3) 11:00–11:30 PT: Short break / instrumentation check
4) 11:30–12:30 PT: Load/throughput window (we'll run sustained scenarios and capture latency distributions)

Action items for OptiScale before the session:
- Share the prompt bundle and any golden outputs you want preserved for quality checks (I got the zip).
- Confirm target throughput (you mentioned ~4k tokens/sec) and whether tokens/sec is measured per cluster or per customer tenant.

Looping in Marissa (CS lead) and Sean (perf lead) to prepare the test harness and runbook. We'll attach a draft agenda and the load script for your review.

Diego
Diego Fernandez
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: poc-agenda.pdf (PDF)]

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-17T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: POC kickoff — availability and high-level asks

Team — forwarding OptiScale's asks. Key points:

- They want sustained ~4k tokens/sec for a 16-concurrent-user fanout.
- p95 latency target <250ms at 256 tokens.
- Need to demo routing fallback and quantized model behavior.

Please prep:
- Sean: can you adapt our load-script.yaml to produce the requested token/sec profile and produce a preflight run that simulates warm cache vs cold cache? Attachments: load-script.yaml (draft) and kv-routing-matrix.csv (mapping for prompt->model variants).
- Marissa: runbook + monitoring playbook; we'll keep a quality gate using the golden outputs. Monica — please coordinate customer invites and calendar block.

I'll schedule the 3-hour block for July 31 09:00–12:00 PT pending OptiScale confirmation. If we need more than one load window, we'll add a 4pm fallback.

Diego

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-18T11:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: POC kickoff — availability and high-level asks

Diego / team — quick status update from performance prep:

- I've instrumented load-script.yaml to produce two profiles:
  * profile-A: 16 concurrent users, staggered arrival, target 4k tokens/sec cluster-wide (steady-state 10m)
  * profile-B: bursty traffic (50 reqs/s peaks) to validate autoscale + graceful degradation
- Will run a dry run on July 29 in our staging lab (not customer-facing) to validate dataset warm/cold behavior. Results posted to the Drive link.
- For the routing demo, kv-routing-matrix.csv contains mapping logic for fallback to q3-quant models when GPU queue depth exceeds threshold. I added comments about expected latency deltas.

Notes / ask for Marissa: we should preserve a short quality check script that compares sample generated outputs against the golden outputs Alex sent and fail the test if quality drifts >5%. That will be our regression gate during the load window.

I'll attach the draft load-script and small runbook excerpt here.

—Sean
Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: load-script.yaml (YAML)]

From: Cara Lin <cara@optiscale.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-19T14:55:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC: Hands-on throughput playback & prompt routing session

Diego / team — confirmed July 31 09:00–12:00 PT for the session, thank you. A couple of clarifications from our side before the workshop:

- Measurement scope: throughput measured cluster-wide is fine; please tag the results with the tenant identifier so we can map to our multi-tenant billing model.
- Quality gate: we'll approve the >95% pass on the golden-output check as the go/no-go signal for the final demo.
- Security ask: can you provide a minimal audit log snippet post-run that shows request IDs and model variant chosen? We just need anonymized rows (no user PII).

I've uploaded an updated prompt set and a short SOC note. Attaching the SOC snippet and prompt bundle.

See you on the 31st — Alex will join the workshop and I'll run the business Q&A at the end.

Best,
Cara Lin
Program Manager, OptiScale
[Attachment: optiscale-prompt-bundle-v2.zip (zip), optiscale-soc-note.pdf (PDF)]
